page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top left, page number at top right. Main text in one column, with marginal notes in the right margin beside the first paragraph and beside the second paragraph. No text below the main text.

main_text.p: Quod vero ad alterum fidei & Salutis meae caput, & consolationis basin attinet, iidem illi homines, Doctrinam de Merito & Satisfactione JESU CHRISTI expresse humanum commentum vocitare solent. Audent aperte disputare, Falsam esse sententiam istam, quod Christum morte sua Deo, sive ejus justitiae pro peccatis nostris satisfecerit: quia in Deo satis sit misericordiae ad nos absque ulla satisfactione salvandos: imo Deum jure potuisse nobis condonare peccata nostra, nulla vera pro ipsis satisfactione ab ulla persona, ullove modo accepta. Item contendunt constanter, Christum poenarum, quas nos subire, ex lege Dei, tenebamur, solutione divina justitia pro nobis satisfacere non potuisse: Nullo pacto Christi satisfactione per fidem nobis imputari: imo Christi justitiam nobis imputare, merum esse commentum.

Deum quidem satis misericordem esse ad condonanda mihi peccata mea non ambigo; at interim si Christus Sponsor, si Sponsoris hujus Meritum & satisfactio mihi eripitur, profecto quantum ex Sacris Scripturis, & me ipso

page.notes: Marginal notes, not transcribed in full: beside the first paragraph, a note in italic, "Secundi fun-damenti la-befactio Neariana." (the last word reads Neariana [?]). Beside the second paragraph, notes of the form "Auctoris ..." and "pofino & pefsino" are only partly legible and are not transcribed. A small "31" stands near the running head; it is probably a printer's or folio mark and is not given as page number. The top-right number "234" is uncertain at the last digit.
